description.narrative: Increased support to infoDev's multi donor trust fund 2013-2019. Last disbursement of current funding was made in 2014.

InfoDEV MDTF är en 'multi donor trust fund' som administreras och implementeras av Världbankens enhet för Innovation och Entreprenörskap. Målsättningen med infoDEV MDTF är att främja konkurrenskraft, sysselsättning, och hållbar inkluderande tillväxt inom sektorerna digitalt entreprenörskap, jordbruk och klimat genom att: (i) testa nya tillvägagångssätt som möjliggör tillväxt av innovativa företag; ii) generera och sprida kunskap; och (iii) stärka partners kapacitet att utforma och genomföra program som möjliggör tillväxt av innovativa företag.
InfoDEV MDTF är en partner med ett globalt nätverk av innovationshubbar (mLabs) och centra för innovation. InfoDEV MDTF positionerar sig från andra aktörer på det sätt som fonden fokuserar på att stärka lokala institutioners kapacitet. På mikronivå är entreprenörer / små / medelstora företag primära mottagare av stöd.
Aktiviteter genomförs genom de tre programmen Digital Entrepreneurship Programme, Agribusiness Entrepreneurship Programme, och Climate Technology Programme. InfoDEV MDTF har ett starkt genderfokus som integreras i alla program och aktiviteter.

InfoDev is a multi-donor trust fund (MDTF) that supports entrepreneurs in developing economies to expand their scale and reach in order to, ultimately, contribute to development and poverty alleviation. It is implemented by the World Bank Groups Firm, Entrepreneurship and innovation unit and Markets and Technology unit under the Finance, Competitiveness and Innovation (FCI) global practice.
It oversees a global network of business incubators and innovation hubs for climate technology, agribusiness, and digital entrepreneurs. Through Climate Innovation Centers, Mobile Application Labs (mLabs), and Agribusiness Entrepreneurship Centers, it connects entrepreneurs with the knowledge, funding, and markets they need to grow their businesses.
The objectives of the infoDEV MDTF are to promote competitiveness, employment and sustainable, inclusive growth in the mobile, agribusiness and climate technology sectors by:
- testing new approaches that enable the growth of innovative new ventures;
- creating and disseminating knowledge; and
-strengthening recipients' capacity to design and implement programs that enable the growth of innovative new ventures.

description.narrative:
A final evaluation in line with the procedures of the Bank has been conducted in 2021 and published in November. The evaluation was conducted from June to November 2021 using a mixed-methods and theory-based approach. The evaluation team leveraged a variety of tools to collect and analyze primary and secondary sources of qualitative data, including document review, key informant interviews and focus group discussions.
The approach was guided by the OECD/DAC Criteria for Evaluating Development Assistance and the UN Evaluation Group (UNEG) best practices. The approach was also designed to reflect the Principles, Guidelines and Good Practices of the World Banks Independent Evaluation Group. The evaluation looks at issues related to: 1) Effectiveness; 2) Efficiency; 3) Relevance; 4) coherence and 5) sustainability. The evaluation provides good examples of what have been achieved, and problems/ challenges involved in the course of the implementation. Here under are some of the findings from the final evaluation report and results achieved.
1) The infoDev MDTF has met or exceeded almost all targets set at the time of program design. There is evidence to support that the MDTF has partially achieved immediate outcomes by increasing the reach of business enablers and MDTF learnings being leveraged by WBG and achieved intermediate outcomes by enabling the growth of SMEs. However, there is limited evidence to conclude whether the ultimate outcome (i.e., GO entrepreneurs contributing to poverty alleviation) was achieved.
2)The infoDev MDTF has been successful at enabling the growth and innovation of domestic SMEs and improving the enabling environment by increasing SMEs access to financing, supporting SMEs in attracting direct private investments, and establishing public policies to support the entrepreneurial environment. MDTF provisioned domestic SMEs with financial capital in the form of investments which helped SMEs scale-up production, establish production sites, and expand operations locally which contributed to increased sales and profits. These funds were also used to strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems in targeted regions which attracted local and foreign investors to further support SMEs in accessing financing mechanisms. Finally, MDTF influenced policies that encouraged the growth and stimulation of entrepreneurship and innovation in targeted regions.
3) At the impact level, infoDev MDTF aims to support poverty alleviation through the scale and reach of GO businesses expanding and contributing to national economic development. Currently, there is limited evidence to conclude on the programs contribution to the achievement of poverty alleviation outcomes. However, since the program has created jobs (directly and indirectly), it has the potential to contribute to poverty alleviation in the households of beneficiaries.
4) Overall, infoDev MDTF has been successful at leveraging a small amount of funding and translating funding into the development of a wider entrepreneurship ecosystem and other WBG lending operations. Teams were able to overcome capacity and budgetary limitations to generate larger outputs by leveraging online tools, human resources, and social capital. The WBG also enhanced efficiency by incorporating feedback to streamline administrative processes which prevented the occurrence of bottlenecks and delays. This strategic direction resulted in the expansion of MDTF investments by scaling solutions into larger WBG initiatives.
5) The infoDev MDTF was aligned to the needs of national priorities as it was the first initiative across many countries to help establish ecosystems for entrepreneurs to grow and trigger dialogue across partners and government agencies. Through the programmatic efforts of MDTF, entrepreneurial ecosystems were developed within targeted regions which triggered momentum and interest in the digital and agroprocessing sectors. These efforts contributed to the regional development of new markets, stimulation of local economies, and attraction of private investment.
6) InfoDev MDTF was relevant to the needs of partners as the WBGs support provided credibility and stimulus for partners to obtain government support and drive action. Through partnership with MDTF, donors, development partners, and implementing partners were able to execute initiatives that aligned with their shared goals of innovation and economic development. These partnerships often resulted in synergies through shared resources and learnings which increased impact and attracted the support of local government agencies.
7) InfoDev MDTF was a pioneer for entrepreneurship in regions/countries of implementation. Initially, the program did not have a strategy for sectoral coherence and was not complementary to other initiatives as they did not exist. However, as the ecosystem grew and the entrepreneurship space became more saturated, the program was open to working with other programs within target sectors to pool resources. In doing so, the program established sectoral partnerships with compatible organizations to help deliver program outcomes and establish collective support (i.e., sharing facilities and co-working spaces)
8) The infoDev MDTF has made efforts to the sustainability of program outcomes by supporting some implementing partners and beneficiaries in the development of business plans that include consideration of sustainable revenue diversification. In doing so, some enablers were able to sustain operations and limit dependence on external sources of financing (i.e., public subsidies). Further, some infoDev MDTF-funded initiatives resulted in spillover effects that translated to sustained outcomes such as the creation of ecosystems that sustain the growth of future SMEs and graduates of training programs entering industry-specific careers.
In summary the Evaluation Team found that infoDev MDTF has been effective at building the skills and capacity of early-stage and GO entrepreneurs, increasing the reach of enablers, and improving access to finance for GO SMEs. While it is too early to assess the programs overall impact on poverty reduction, there is evidence to suggest that the programme may eventually contribute to poverty alleviation in the households of beneficiaries through the creation of direct and indirect jobs. The program was relevant to the needs of program beneficiaries, national priorities, and donors/development partners by the providing facilities to areas with limited resources, triggering national policy dialogue to strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems, and sharing goals surrounding innovation and economic development in fragile countries. Overall, the program has been efficient at converting limited inputs into larger outputs by mobilizing and leveraging existing resources to maximize outcomes. These efforts have often resulted in spillover effects such as contributing to the design of larger, scalable lending operations. As of FY20, the infoDev MDTF contributed to $2.4 billion in World Bank lending toward shared priority areas. The program has been instrumental in informing and embedding different design components to ensure greater outreach and scale. Nevertheless, there were opportunities to improve program implementation such as better integration of gender equality considerations, streamlining processes to enhance operational and cost-efficiency, and identifying continued sources of funding to sustain operations beyond program completion despite the efforts placed on sustainable revenue diversification. While the programme has delivered the above results, it is important to note that there were several challenges which the programme had to face. Political factors, implementing partner capacity, gender norms, ecosystem capacity, the program delivery model, and impacts of COVID-19 acted as hindering factors which had to be addressed during the course of implementation.
